core.title: Assign each component's layer from its artifact type and responsibility
core.given: A planned component has an artifact type (events, states, data or configs) and a responsibility.
core.when: The planner assigns, changes or reassesses its layer, or its responsibility changes.
core.then: Assign a layer from the artifact type's typical layers, chosen by responsibility: events → integration|application; states → domain|application; data → domain|application|integration; configs → application|integration.
prefer: Events (publishers sit at boundaries): publishing to external systems → integration; emitting internal events → application.
States: tracking core business state → domain; coordinating state/lifecycle → application.
Data (spans layers by responsibility): business logic → domain; coordinating the workflow → application; persisting to a store → integration.
Configs: coordinating setup → application; loading settings (e.g. from an external config store) → integration.
Treat the mapping as the default, defensible placement, not an absolute prohibition — findings are reported but do not block.
avoid: Placing an external event publisher in the domain layer.
Deciding the layer case by case or from the component name alone, ignoring its responsibility.
core.why: A typical-layer mapping per artifact type gives a default, defensible placement for each component, so layer assignment is consistent rather than guessed case by case.
evidence: The layer-assignment check for the plan's components passes (advisory: findings are reported, not blocking).

Each component's layer is in its artifact type's typical-layer set and the stated responsibility matches the chosen layer (boundary/external or settings loading/persistence → integration, coordination → application, core business state/logic → domain).
Compliant example: a state tracker placed in the domain layer. Non-compliant: an external event publisher placed in the domain layer.
verification: A layer-assignment check scans the planned components: each component's layer, resolved to its layer role using the stack's layer names (profile: roles.layers), must fall within its artifact type's typical-layer set (events: integration, application; states: domain, application; data: domain, application, integration; configs: application, integration).

The check mechanically verifies only membership in the typical-layer set; that the stated responsibility matches the chosen layer is judged from the plan's own component statement (see evidence), and the file-kind activation examples are illustrative, not an exhaustive gate.
Advisory disposition (severity 2): findings are reported but do not block.
The concrete validator, finding and term identifiers of this rule are realization details; the core names the check generically.

facts.note: Fires while the planner authors or revises component entries; the planning phase must be exposed by the harness.

Illustrative examples only, not an exhaustive gate: any planner artifact that declares a component with an artifact type, responsibility or layer qualifies. The stack's concrete plan-artifact kinds come from the profile.
Diff-level fact: a component entry is added, its layer/artifact type/responsibility is edited, or an existing placement is being reviewed.
Task text mentions components, their responsibility or layer placement.
The layer-assignment check reports a component whose layer is outside its artifact type's typical layers.

fires: Planner adds an event-publisher component and must choose its layer
Planner declares a state-tracker component and sets its layer
Planner changes a config component's layer or artifact type
Planner changes a component's responsibility (e.g. a data component goes from coordinating a workflow to persisting to a store), so its existing placement must be reassessed
Planner reviews existing component placements in a plan
The layer-assignment check flags an external event publisher assigned to the domain layer
doesNotFire: Coder edits implementation code without touching planned component layer assignments
Planner edits acceptance wording that changes neither the component's responsibility nor its artifact type or layer
Checking that a component has exactly one layer (covered by planner.component.layer-consistency)

neutralityNotes: The typical-layer mapping and the events/states/data/configs artifact-type taxonomy are convention content, not stack facts, and reference only layer-role names, so they stay in the core. The stack contributes data through the profile: how layer roles are spelled in plans (roles.layers, e.g. side-qualified backend.domain) and the concrete plan-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds, e.g. product capability, desired outcome). Named component examples (MatchStartedPublisher, TimebankTracker, Choice*, ConfigLoader), the validator/finding ids and the sidecar term-registry ids/labels are bunOnly; bun.json itself remains the worked reference example. Per-rule advisory disposition and severity 2 are kept in core verification, not the profile. The doesNotFire cross-reference to the sibling planner.component.layer-consistency rule is kept as a convention-level reference. Nothing in the obligation resisted neutralization.
